answer: A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases as a result has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. Because the trellis collateral is checked against the tide claim at intake, the spiral audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. Posted collateral must equal 6 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. That is 6 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
